extracted.intended_audience: State, local, and Indian tribal governments and other entities governed by OMB Circular A-87 that receive or administer U.S. Department of Education (ED) grants
extracted.subtask_short: time distribution records for ED grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for documenting and supporting charges for salaries and related costs to U.S. Department of Education grants for entities governed by OMB Circular A-87, including acceptable time distribution records, substitute systems, certification, monitoring, and consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payroll documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to an ED grant for salaries and wages, whether direct or indirect, must be based on payrolls documented in accordance with generally accepted practices of the recipient state or local agency and approved by a responsible official of that agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payrolls must be supported by time and attendance or equivalent records for individuals; payroll documentation is a foundational requirement distinct from time distribution records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time distribution records requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee works on more than one program or cost objective, a distribution of the employee's salaries or wages is acceptable only if supported by time distribution records that meet the standards in paragraph (3) or by an approved substitute system under paragraph (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when employees work on multiple ED grants, multiple cost objectives under an ED grant, an ED grant and other federal/non-federal programs; time distribution systems are in addition to payroll documentation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy — actual time, not budget estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must accurately reflect a distribution of the actual time spent on each activity by each employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not accept budget estimates or other distributions determined before the services are performed as support for charges to an ED grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for total activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must account for the total activity for which each employee is compensated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should reflect the full set of duties and activities paid by the employer so that all compensated time is allocated among cost objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous preparation (monthly minimum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must be prepared contemporaneously at least monthly and summarize the distribution of the employee's activity for the month in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly records are acceptable if the employee relies on supporting documentation (calendars, class schedules, travel vouchers, work product) and entries are made to the best of the employee's knowledge and belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification — signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records must be signed by the employee or by a supervisory official who has first-hand knowledge of the activities performed by the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature provides attestation to the accuracy of the contemporaneous records; supervisory signature allowed if the supervisor has first-hand knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical employee time accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical employees may account for time by (i) basing records on the time distribution of a single employee they serve, or (ii) basing records on the time distribution of each employee served adjusted through a reasonable averaging method if they serve multiple employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows simplified approaches for typical clerical duties, provided the averaging method is reasonable and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable allocation when time cannot be divided
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an employee performs functions on a specific project that benefit more than one program/cost objective and is unable to divide time between them because of the nature of the project, costs may be charged on a basis other than time spent provided charges are equitably distributed among funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must develop and maintain justification and the basis for the allocation when the method is adopted. Examples: prorating costs for a single manual among grants based on proportion of funds; prorating a teacher's class between programs based on student proportions; allocations should change when underlying proportions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute systems — certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In place of time distribution records, a recipient may use a substitute system (e.g., statistical sampling) if, prior to charging federal funds, it obtains certification from an independent public accounting firm or qualified auditor that the system (i) is consistent with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and with the standards in paragraph (4)(d), and (ii) provides distribution of costs equitable to the government and the programs in accordance with OMB Circular A-87, taking into account benefit actually derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must be by an independent auditor who meets GAO Government Auditing Standards independence requirements; substitute systems must equitably allocate costs among funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification documentation and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification must describe the system employed and be available for inspection by the Secretary or designee, together with the supporting documentation upon which the certification was based; record retention rules apply to the certification and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must retain the certification and underlying documentation for the applicable retention period and make them available for audit/inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of allowable substitute systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute systems may include random sampling, case counts, client counts, transaction counts, or other quantifiable measures of employee effort for a time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling and other measures should take into account relative effort or intensity of service between different categories of clients served; substitute systems must translate measures into time-equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling standards for substitute systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A sampling-based substitute system must meet acceptable statistical sampling standards, including: (i) universe includes all employees to be allocated by sampling; (ii) entire time period covered; (iii) results statistically valid and applied only to applicable time period; (iv) results periodically updated to reflect changes; (v) use a valid and uniform system for converting measures into time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling systems must be statistically defensible, updated, and include valid conversion methods; periodic updates required when case/client measures change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and audit prohibition for certifying firm
rubrics_metrics.description: A public accounting firm or qualified auditor that provides certification for a substitute system may not also audit the certification or the system in connection with an organization-wide or single audit under OMB Circular A-128.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflicts of interest between certification and subsequent audit of the same system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written requests for guidance and reliance protection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency has a question about its time distribution system or the allowability of expenditures, it may write to the U.S. Department of Education for guidance pursuant to section 453 of the General Education Provisions Act; written guidance reasonably relied upon by an agency may be used to reduce or eliminate liability for a future finding of unallowable expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures in Section 453 and 34 C.F.R. 81.23 for full details; obtaining written guidance provides some protection from later disallowances if reasonably relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and audit of systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Time distribution records systems described in paragraph (3) or substitute systems approved under paragraph (4) are subject to monitoring and subsequent audit to ensure proper implementation and that the system works as designed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Department reviews a bona fide certified substitute system, it may provide further guidance or direction, but will not question prior costs incurred in accordance with the proper implementation of a bona fide certified system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards for certifying auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent public accounting firm or qualified auditor that provides the certification must use due professional care and operate within the standards of professional ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will take steps to ensure adherence to professional ethics and due care by certifying firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to meet requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a grantee fails to keep time distribution records in accordance with paragraph (3) or fails to establish and maintain a pre-approved substitute system under paragraph (4), or otherwise fails to satisfy the requirement, the Department takes an audit exception and recovers funds proportionate to the harm to an identifiable Federal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantee failing to keep records or maintain a satisfactory system is subject to audit and potential recovery of funds under statutory authority (see 20 U.S.C. 1234b(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing review, flexibility, and presumption of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines contain acceptable but not exclusive approaches; Department officials regard compliance with these guidelines as compliance with the Circular A-87 time distribution requirement; recipients may adopt other alternatives to meet the requirement; the Department will closely review the operation of this non-regulatory guidance to ensure accountability and flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines are non-regulatory, provide safe-harbor approaches, and allow innovation provided accountability is preserved; Department retains oversight to assess effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines are effective on issuance and are applicable to pending cases except where an advance certification is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should apply the guidelines immediately upon issuance unless a specific advance certification is needed.
